events.promise: A bounded test with one real SaaS offer will let the reader judge whether MarketingOS's source-grounded drafting and cold-reader review produce an email worth using and reveal exactly what still needs correction.
events.arc: Email 1 moves the reader from having an invited account to running the smallest useful test: one real offer and one email. Email 2 moves them from judging the prose at face value to examining the source facts and reader feedback that explain what the draft claimed, what failed to land and what should be kept or revised.

emails.job: Get the invited tester to run the smallest useful test with one real SaaS offer.
emails.single_idea: Do not begin with a full campaign: sign in, add the real material for one offer and request one launch or onboarding email that can be judged against that material.
emails.objection: A full generation run may be more evaluation than the reader wants before seeing whether the output fits a real offer; answer by keeping the first request to one email, without claiming that the run will be fast or effortless.
must_not_say: Do not describe this as public signup, a free trial or a purchase.
Do not mention a price, discount, plan or continuation terms.
Do not promise that the draft will outperform existing copy, save time or be ready to send unchanged.
Do not assume what writing tools, sending platform, team structure, list size or campaign results the reader has.
Do not introduce competitor research, audience research, LinkedIn outreach or contact finding in this email.
Do not reuse claims from the older orqAgent agent-builder product, including agents, Slack bots, integrations or credits.
emails.felt_need: I need a launch or onboarding campaign for a real SaaS offer, but I first need to see whether this product can produce one usable email from the material I actually have.
emails.mechanism: MarketingOS accepts a website, PDF, screenshot or pasted material and a request in the user's own words. The reader can therefore test it with one real offer and one specific email request rather than inventing a sample project or committing to a complete sequence.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing MarketingOS account, add the website, PDF, screenshot or pasted material for one real offer, and request one launch or onboarding email.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the first draft is relevant enough to justify testing the rest of the campaign workflow.
emails.next_step_value: The existing account provides the place to register the brand, add real offer material and generate a reviewed email draft from a request written in the reader's own words.
emails.next_step_limit: This first run does not establish campaign performance, sector-wide quality, pricing or whether the draft can be sent without the reader checking it.

emails.job: Teach the tester how to review the run and ask them to inspect the evidence and feedback behind the draft.
emails.single_idea: The useful review is not limited to whether the email sounds polished: inspect the source facts to see what the draft was allowed to claim, then inspect the unfamiliar reader's feedback to see what did not land.
emails.objection: The reader still has to check every draft, and factual errors may still occur. Answer by presenting the source facts and reader feedback as inspection aids—not guarantees—and by making errors and required edits part of the requested pilot review.
must_not_say: Do not claim that the compiled facts prevent all factual errors.
Do not imply that cold-reader review proves conversions, opens, clicks or revenue.
Do not say the draft is approved, final or safe to send without checking facts, links and brand voice.
Do not claim that the product sends, publishes or installs the campaign in another tool.
Do not ask for a testimonial, public endorsement or purchase.
Do not introduce pricing, competitive analysis, audience discovery, contact finding or LinkedIn features.
Do not reuse claims from the older orqAgent agent-builder product.
emails.felt_need: I need to know which parts of this draft are grounded, which parts are unclear to someone new to the offer and what I would have to change before using it.
emails.status_quo: A draft can be judged only as finished prose—whether it sounds plausible—without separating factual grounding from reader comprehension.
emails.why_it_fails: Fluent prose does not reveal whether a claim came from the supplied material or whether a reader unfamiliar with the product understood the argument; those are different failure modes and call for different edits.
emails.mechanism: MarketingOS first compiles the supplied material into facts it is allowed to claim, then has the draft read by someone unfamiliar with the product and rewrites what did not land. Reviewing those source facts and that reader response lets the tester distinguish a factual mismatch from an explanation that is merely unclear, then report the phrases worth keeping or rewriting, factual errors and editing time.
emails.call_to_action: Sign in to your existing account and review the source facts, unfamiliar-reader feedback and draft for the same real offer, noting phrases you would keep or rewrite, factual errors and editing time.
emails.next_step_decision: Decide whether the draft is grounded and clear enough to continue with the rest of the launch or onboarding campaign.
emails.next_step_value: The review exposes the two inputs needed for that decision: the allowed source facts behind the claims and the response of a reader who did not already know the product, alongside the specific pilot notes requested.
emails.next_step_limit: This inspection does not prove commercial performance or remove the need to check facts, links and brand voice before transferring any text into a sending tool.

events.subject: Check what the draft supports
events.preview_text: Separate factual mismatches from explanations that did not land.
events.body:
MarketingOS lets you inspect a draft against the source facts behind its claims and the response of a reader unfamiliar with the offer. Use both checks before deciding what is usable.

The source facts show what the supplied material allowed MarketingOS to claim. They do not prevent every error, but they help you identify a factual mismatch instead of judging the draft only by how plausible it sounds.

The unfamiliar-reader feedback reveals a different problem: where the argument or explanation was unclear to someone without prior product knowledge. MarketingOS uses that response to rewrite what did not land, giving you specific language to assess rather than a first draft alone.

In your existing account, review those two inputs beside the draft for the same real offer. Note the phrases you would keep or rewrite, factual errors and editing time, then check the facts, links and brand voice before transferring any text to your sending tool.

events.preview_text: Use two checks to decide what is usable and what needs revision.
events.body:
Reading a draft only as finished prose leaves two questions tangled together: which claims came from the supplied material, and where someone new to the offer lost the argument. Fluency alone cannot separate a factual mismatch from an unclear explanation.

MarketingOS is an email campaign drafting application that exposes both checks. Its source facts show what the draft was allowed to claim; the unfamiliar-reader feedback shows which parts did not land before the rewrite.

Inspect both alongside the draft for the same real offer. A source mismatch calls for a factual correction; a reader’s confusion points to an explanation that needs revising. These are inspection aids, not guarantees of accuracy or performance.

Sign in to your existing account and record the language you would retain or revise, any factual errors and the time spent editing. Check the facts, links and brand voice before transferring any text into your sending tool.
